label: first copy step (re-input of token 0) in short sequences starting with k/l/y/2 that contain b or m
explanation: Sparse feature. 81% of activation mass is at recall_idx==1, the step right after <DEL> where the first original token is fed back in and token 1 is output. It is strongly skewed to short sequences (L=3: 27x lift, L=4: 4.5x lift). Rate depends on the first token (k, l, y, 2 dominate, with weaker b, e, 1) and on whether b or m appears among the original tokens (as the token being output next, or as the last original token). The strongest examples are L=3 sequences like l b m, l b b, k b m. There is a small tail (~16% of mass) late in the original phase (t=3..5), usually on tokens after b/m/i/g. It almost never fires at t<3, during later copy steps, or when copying has gone wrong. The conjunction is a combinatorial lookup over token identities rather than one clean concept: even the best predicate has low precision, because most short k/l/y/2-initial sequences with b/m do not fire. Magnitude is highest for L=3 sequences that have b/m in positions 1-2.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: L=3 & t=4 (+7.27), orig0=k (+4.57), prev_tok=i (+4.46), prev_tok=g (+4.27), t=5 & prev_tok=<DEL> (+4.10), in_tok=y (+3.23). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.11), orig_idx=-1 (-3.09), orig1=i (-2.88), orig2=t (-2.80).
